note_en: The idiom 三天打鱼两天晒网, literally "fish for three days, dry the nets for two," describes someone who keeps starting and stopping, never sticking with anything. In 千万不要三天打鱼两天晒网 it works like an English verb phrase ("never do things in fits and starts"), and it pairs naturally with another four-character idiom in the same sentence, 半途而废 "give up halfway." Chinese often packs a whole image into a fixed phrase like this, where English would use a plain verb such as "slack off."
